title: 21 Things You Should Do To Students
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Written as a companion piece to the previous week's 'never do' article, Linsin explains that SCM runs counter to many popular classroom management approaches, including PBIS, and that his goal is not to disparage other methods but to give teachers real, doable strategies centered on students' long-term development. He presents a list of 21 things teachers should do, each linking to a fuller article, covering areas such as removing excitability, being consistently kind, holding students accountable, building rapport, and giving worthy praise. He stresses that new readers may find items vague out of context and should follow the links, since a decade of supporting articles underlies each concept. The piece closes by emphasizing that the 21 practices are meant to be used together as a unified, aligned approach rather than piecemeal, distinguishing SCM from the 'hodge-podge' of conflicting advice many teachers try.
points: SCM's approach is explicitly positioned as running counter to popular classroom-management methods, including PBIS.
A 21-item list of recommended teacher practices is presented, each tied to a fuller supporting article on the site.
New readers are cautioned that individual list items may seem vague without the broader context of the SCM approach.
Linsin emphasizes the practices are meant to be used together as a unified system, not selected piecemeal.
The unified approach is credited with reducing teacher stress, building intrinsic motivation, and bringing peace to classrooms, according to reader feedback.
